result.note: Tested the port involved and the details of India's diplomatic response; the wider foreign-policy reading is left to the explanations.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, India lodged a protest with Russia after a missile strike killed four Indian crew members aboard the cargo vessel MV Golden Leo. The ship was departing which port when it was attacked?
questions.explain: The Golden Leo was attacked on the evening of 19 July 2026 while leaving Ukraine's Odessa port. Five of its 17 crew were Indian nationals, and one survivor is in a critical condition.
questions.source: On the evening of July 19, 2026, the cargo vessel Golden Leo was attacked while departing Odessa.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's response to the July 2026 missile strike on the MV Golden Leo:
items: The Ministry of External Affairs summoned Russia's Chargé d'Affaires in New Delhi.
Ukraine's Navy said Russian forces launched three cruise missiles at the ship.
It was the first time in 2026 that India had protested to a foreign power over the deaths of seafarers.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong because this was the third such protest in six weeks. India had earlier summoned the United States twice and Iran once over crew losses during the Iran war. The MEA conveyed its 'grave concerns and unequivocal condemnation' to Chargé d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov, a notable step given that Russia is one of India's closest partners.
questions.source: This is the third time in six weeks India has protested a foreign power over dead seafarers.
